correctness.rationale: The proof treats exactly \(r=1,2,3\) prime-power blocks. For \(r=1\) the equation reduces to \((M-1)N=2\). For \(r=2\) the exact ratio bound forces \(M=2\) and then \((A-1)(B-1)=3\), incompatible with coprimality. For \(r=3\) the maximal ratio \(12/5\) forces \(M=2\); the resulting linear formula for the largest block is closed in the cases \(A=2\), \(A=3\), and \(A\ge4\). The last case is ruled out by a strictly positive monotone difference \(D(A,B)\), so the proof has no finite-search gap.

value.rationale: The equation is a natural signed companion to a longstanding unitary Lehmer analogue. An exact support threshold is structurally useful because the principal modern bounds are asymptotic or quantitative and do not resolve these low-support repeated-exponent cases. The result is a complete, unbounded classification of the first three support layers rather than a numerical cutoff or arbitrary parameter slice.
